```{r setup, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
options(width = 76)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 5.4, out.width = "100%", dpi = 96)
# Cut each figure to a palette of 256 colours, about a third of its size with
# no visible change, because the built vignettes ship in the tarball
if (requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE)) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.process = function(path) {
    img <- magick::image_quantize(magick::image_read(path), max = 256,
                                  colorspace = "sRGB", dither = FALSE)
    magick::image_write(img, path, format = "png")
    path
  })
}
# Numbers for the prose: metres to two decimals, coefficients to three,
# ratios to two, shares as whole percentages
m2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
dec <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
ratio <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
```

```{r intro-numbers, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# The finding the first paragraph states, read from the included study
intro_hours <- detfield::stoney_selection$hours
intro_shift <- mean(intro_hours$drawn_m - intro_hours$true_m)
intro_trial <- detfield::stoney_selection$trial
shallow_ratio <- sapply(1:2, function(b) {
  rows <- intro_trial[intro_trial$block == b & intro_trial$receivers == 70 &
                        intro_trial$availability == "weighted" &
                        intro_trial$beta == -0.3, ]
  mean(rows$estimate[rows$source == "positions"]) /
    mean(rows$estimate[rows$source == "truth"])
})
```

Hourly location surfaces can be used in a habitat-selection analysis: the positions of an animal in
the hours it was heard are set against the water available to it, to ask which depths it used
more than their availability. This page tests that use on simulated animals whose preference
for depth is known, comparing the answer from position estimates with the answer from the
true track. A position draw is one water cell drawn from an hour's location surface with
probability equal to the cell's posterior probability, so a set of draws from each detected
hour represents the hour's uncertainty in the analysis ([the
model](positioning.html#the-model)). The page needs the **survival** R package for the
conditional logit; [Get started](detfield.html) shows how
the surfaces behind the draws are built.

On average, position draws from hourly surfaces put a simulated animal
`r m2(intro_shift)` m deeper than it was, most in water 1 m deep or less, and a preference for
shallow water comes back at about half its size (`r ratio(shallow_ratio[1])` and
`r ratio(shallow_ratio[2])` of the true track's coefficient in two blocks of animals). This
page shows both on `stoney_selection`, 40 animals simulated for 48 hours on 70 Stoney Lake
receivers, with availability drawn from the array's detection surface as in positionR 1.x.

```{r depth-shift}
# Attach detfield, survival for the conditional logit, and ggplot2
library(detfield)
library(survival)
library(ggplot2)
# Hour by hour on 70 receivers: the mean bottom depth of the 20 position
# draws minus that of the 20 true points (every third minute)
trial_hours <- stoney_selection$hours
trial_hours$shift_m <- trial_hours$drawn_m - trial_hours$true_m
trial_hours$band <- cut(trial_hours$true_m, c(-Inf, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, Inf),
                        labels = c("1 m or less", "1 to 2.5 m", "2.5 to 5 m",
                                   "5 to 10 m", "over 10 m"))
shift_by_band <- aggregate(shift_m ~ block + band, data = trial_hours,
                           FUN = function(m) c(mean = mean(m), hours = length(m)))
shift_by_band <- do.call(data.frame, shift_by_band)
names(shift_by_band) <- c("block", "band", "mean_m", "hours")
shift_by_band$mean_m <- round(shift_by_band$mean_m, 2)
shift_by_band
# Hours beyond 6 m either way, which the figure's axis cuts off
sum(abs(trial_hours$shift_m) > 6)
```

```{r plot-depth-shift, fig.height = 4.4, fig.alt = "Boxplots of the hourly difference in bottom depth between position draws and the true position, by the depth of the true position, for two blocks of simulated animals; the difference is largest in water 1 m deep or less."}
# Draw the hourly differences by true depth band, one panel per block
ggplot(trial_hours, aes(band, shift_m)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, outlier.alpha = 0.4, fill = "grey92",
               colour = "grey35") +
  stat_summary(aes(colour = "Mean"), fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 2.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = c(Mean = "#2C5AA0")) +
  facet_wrap(~ block, labeller = as_labeller(c(`1` = "Block 1",
                                               `2` = "Block 2"))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-6, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Bottom depth at the true position",
       y = "Draws minus true position (m)") +
  theme_positionr() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

*Per detected hour on 70 receivers, mean bottom depth of 20 position draws minus that of the
20 true cells (every third minute); 100 animals per block, 20 at each of five preferences.
`r sum(abs(trial_hours$shift_m) > 6)` of `r format(nrow(trial_hours), big.mark = ",")`
hours lie beyond the 6 m axis limits.*

```{r shift-numbers, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# Numbers the prose quotes, read from the hourly table
shift_mean <- tapply(trial_hours$shift_m, trial_hours$block, mean)
band_value <- function(b, band, what = "mean_m") {
  shift_by_band[shift_by_band$block == b & shift_by_band$band == band, what]
}
single <- trial_hours$receivers == 1
shift_single <- tapply(trial_hours$shift_m[single], trial_hours$block[single],
                       mean)
shift_more <- tapply(trial_hours$shift_m[!single], trial_hours$block[!single],
                     mean)
hours_n <- table(trial_hours$block)
deeper <- tapply(trial_hours$shift_m > 0, trial_hours$block, mean)
mid <- trial_hours$band == "2.5 to 5 m"
deeper_mid <- tapply(trial_hours$shift_m[mid] > 0, trial_hours$block[mid],
                     mean)
# Water over 10 m, by block and preference
deep <- trial_hours[trial_hours$band == "over 10 m", ]
deep_group <- function(b, beta, what) {
  d <- deep[deep$block == b & deep$beta == beta, ]
  if (what == "hours") nrow(d) else mean(d$shift_m)
}
# The example's 40 animals: block 1, beta -0.3 and 0
example <- trial_hours$block == 1 & trial_hours$beta %in% c(-0.3, 0)
example_hours <- sum(example)
example_single <- sprintf("%d (%s)", sum(example & single),
                          pct(sum(example & single) / example_hours))
```

On average the draws read deeper than the true position: by `r m2(shift_mean[["1"]])` m over
the `r format(hours_n[["1"]], big.mark = ",")` detected hours of block 1 and by
`r m2(shift_mean[["2"]])` m over the `r format(hours_n[["2"]], big.mark = ",")` of block 2.
Hour by hour it is less one-sided: `r pct(deeper[["1"]])` and `r pct(deeper[["2"]])` of hours
read deeper, and in water 2.5 to 5 m about half read deeper and half shallower
(`r pct(deeper_mid[["1"]])` and `r pct(deeper_mid[["2"]])` deeper). The mean shift is largest in
water 1 m deep or less, `r m2(band_value(1, "1 m or less"))` m and
`r m2(band_value(2, "1 m or less"))` m, where a draw can only miss toward the open water, which
is deeper. It is no larger in hours heard by one receiver (`r m2(shift_single[["1"]])` m and
`r m2(shift_single[["2"]])` m) than in hours heard by two or more (`r m2(shift_more[["1"]])` m
and `r m2(shift_more[["2"]])` m).

In water over 10 m the mean shift is `r m2(band_value(1, "over 10 m"))` m in block 1 and
`r m2(band_value(2, "over 10 m"))` m in block 2, and it differs by group. In block 2,
`r deep_group(2, 0.3, "hours")` of the `r band_value(2, "over 10 m", "hours")` hours there come
from the animals with beta = +0.3, whose draws read `r m2(deep_group(2, 0.3, "mean"))` m
deeper; the animals with no preference read `r m2(-deep_group(2, 0, "mean"))` m shallower there
(`r deep_group(2, 0, "hours")` hours). The shore explains the shift in shallow water only; the
shift in deep water is not explained.

## The study

`stoney_selection` is a list:

```{r load}
# The parts of the included study, and the animals by preference
study <- stoney_selection
names(study)
table(beta = study$tags$beta)
```

The position draws are the trial's own for these animals: 20 cells per detected hour, drawn
from each hour's location surface with `sample_locations()`. [Get started](detfield.html)
builds the field and the surfaces they come from.

```{r presence}
# One row per animal, detected hour and draw
presence <- study$presence
head(presence, 3)
writeLines(strwrap(attr(presence, "estimand"), 72))
```

## Depth used: true track and position draws

The true points are the animal's cells at every third minute of each detected hour, 20 per
hour; both sets are read on bottom depth:

```{r depth-used}
# Bottom depth in metres from the lake raster
lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                package = "detfield"))
depth <- abs(lake)
names(depth) <- "depth_m"
# The true cells at minutes 0, 3, ..., 57 of an animal's detected hours
true_points <- function(id) {
  minutes <- study$track[study$track$animal_id == id, ]
  minutes$bin_start <- as.POSIXct(trunc(minutes$datetime, "hours"))
  minute <- as.numeric(format(minutes$datetime, "%M"))
  keep <- minutes$bin_start %in% presence$bin_start[presence$animal_id == id] &
    minute %% 3 == 0
  xy <- terra::xyFromCell(lake, minutes$cell[keep])
  data.frame(animal_id = id, bin_start = minutes$bin_start[keep],
             draw = minute[keep] / 3 + 1, cell = minutes$cell[keep],
             x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2])
}
truth <- do.call(rbind, lapply(study$tags$animal_id, true_points))
# Depth of every true point and every draw, with the animal's preference
depth_of_cell <- terra::values(depth, mat = FALSE)
depth_used <- rbind(
  data.frame(animal_id = truth$animal_id, set = "True positions",
             depth_m = depth_of_cell[truth$cell]),
  data.frame(animal_id = presence$animal_id, set = "Position draws",
             depth_m = depth_of_cell[presence$cell])
)
depth_used$beta <- study$tags$beta[match(depth_used$animal_id,
                                         study$tags$animal_id)]
table(depth_used$set)
```

```{r plot-depth-used, fig.height = 8.2, fig.alt = "Per-animal boxplots of bottom depth at the true positions and at the position draws, for 20 animals with a preference for shallow water and 20 with none."}
# Order the animals by their mean true depth, one panel per preference
true_mean <- tapply(depth_used$depth_m[depth_used$set == "True positions"],
                    depth_used$animal_id[depth_used$set == "True positions"],
                    mean)
depth_used$animal_id <- factor(depth_used$animal_id,
                               names(sort(true_mean)))
depth_used$set <- factor(depth_used$set, c("True positions",
                                           "Position draws"))
depth_used$group <- ifelse(depth_used$beta == 0, "No preference (beta 0)",
                           "Shallow preference (beta -0.3)")
ggplot(depth_used, aes(depth_m, animal_id, fill = set)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, outlier.alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2ECC40", "#F28E2B"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "sqrt", breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 30)) +
  labs(x = "Bottom depth (m, square-root scale)",
       y = "Animal, ordered by the mean depth of its true positions") +
  theme_positionr() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7), legend.position = "bottom")
```

*Bottom depth at each animal's true positions and position draws in its detected hours, 20
animals per panel.*

```{r deeper-count}
# Mean depth per animal: true positions against position draws
by_animal <- aggregate(depth_m ~ animal_id + beta + set, data = depth_used,
                       FUN = mean)
by_animal <- reshape(by_animal, idvar = c("animal_id", "beta"),
                     timevar = "set", direction = "wide")
names(by_animal)[names(by_animal) == "depth_m.True positions"] <- "true_m"
names(by_animal)[names(by_animal) == "depth_m.Position draws"] <- "drawn_m"
c(animals = nrow(by_animal),
  draws_deeper = sum(by_animal$drawn_m > by_animal$true_m))
aggregate(cbind(true_m, drawn_m) ~ beta, data = by_animal,
          FUN = function(m) round(mean(m), 2))
# Share of points in water 1 m deep or less, by preference and set
shallow_share <- aggregate(depth_m ~ beta + set, data = depth_used,
                           FUN = function(m) round(mean(m <= 1), 3))
shallow_share
```

```{r shallow-numbers, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# Shares the prose quotes
share_of <- function(b, set) {
  shallow_share$depth_m[shallow_share$beta == b & shallow_share$set == set]
}
```

The draws are deeper than the true positions for `r sum(by_animal$drawn_m > by_animal$true_m)`
of the 40 animals, on the mean of each. The draws under-represent the shallowest water: animals with a
shallow preference spent `r pct(share_of(-0.3, "True positions"))` of their true points in
water 1 m deep or less, and `r pct(share_of(-0.3, "Position draws"))` of their draws fall
there.

## Availability from the detection surface

An hour is a presence only if the animal was heard in it, so availability is drawn in
proportion to the probability that the array detects an hour from each cell. `study$coverage`
holds it per cell and day, `system_de()` with `transmissions = 24`, beside the probability for
one transmission:

```{r coverage}
# Coverage per cell and day: per hour of 24 transmissions, and per
# transmission
coverage <- study$coverage
head(coverage$hour, 3)
max(abs(coverage$hour$p - (1 - (1 - coverage$transmission$p)^24)))
# Share of cell-days from which an hour is detected with p >= 0.95
mean(coverage$hour$p >= 0.95)
```

On this array the weight is close to uniform: `r pct(mean(coverage$hour$p >= 0.95))` of
cell-days are detected with probability 0.95 or more in an hour. `sample_available()` draws 20
cells from that surface for each animal, hour and presence draw:

```{r available}
# Draw 20 available cells per presence draw, with the animal's second seed
available <- lapply(split(study$tags, study$tags$animal_id), function(tag) {
  sample_available(presence[presence$animal_id == tag$animal_id, ],
                   coverage$hour, lake, n = 20, seed = 100 + tag$replicate)
})
head(available[["selection-01"]], 3)
writeLines(strwrap(attr(available[["selection-01"]], "estimand"), 72))
```

`uniform_above` draws uniformly over the cells at or above a probability, here 0.1 per
transmission:

```{r available-uniform}
# Uniform over cells heard with p >= 0.1 per transmission, one animal
uniform <- sample_available(presence[presence$animal_id == "selection-01", ],
                            coverage$transmission, lake, n = 20,
                            uniform_above = 0.1, seed = 101)
writeLines(strwrap(attr(uniform, "estimand"), 72))
# On 1 June: the water cells, those this mode draws from, and those 1.x drew from
june1 <- coverage$transmission[coverage$transmission$date ==
                                 as.Date("2024-06-01"), ]
june1_cells <- c(water = nrow(june1), at_or_above = sum(june1$p >= 0.1),
                 strictly_above = sum(june1$p > 0.1))
june1_cells
```

On 1 June that is `r format(june1_cells[["at_or_above"]], big.mark = ",")` of the
`r format(june1_cells[["water"]], big.mark = ",")` water cells.

```{r map-data}
# One animal with a preference for shallow water: its true track, its
# presence draws and the available cells of its first draw
animal <- "selection-05"
animal_track <- study$track[study$track$animal_id == animal, ]
animal_presence <- presence[presence$animal_id == animal, ]
first_draw <- available[[animal]][available[[animal]]$draw == 1, ]
# Water as a table of cells, depth in metres
depth_cells <- as.data.frame(depth, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
c(hours = length(unique(animal_presence$bin_start)),
  presence = nrow(animal_presence), available = nrow(first_draw))
```

```{r plot-map-lake, fig.height = 5.3, fig.alt = "Map of Stoney Lake with one animal's presence draws in one bay and the available cells of its first draw spread across the lake."}
# The fill scale holds depth, so the key takes the available cells' fill
# from override.aes
point_key <- list(shape = c(21, 19), fill = c("#E7298A", NA), size = c(2, 1.6))
# Map depth, the available cells of draw 1, then the presence draws
ggplot(depth_cells, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = depth_m)) +
  scale_fill_depth() +
  geom_point(data = first_draw, aes(colour = "Available cells, draw 1"),
             shape = 21, fill = "#E7298A", stroke = 0.2, size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = animal_presence, aes(colour = "Presence draws"), size = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("Available cells, draw 1" = "black",
                                 "Presence draws" = "#F28E2B"),
                      guide = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = point_key)) +
  coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Easting (m, UTM 17N)", y = "Northing (m, UTM 17N)") +
  annotation_scale_bar(location = "br") +
  theme_positionr() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

*`r animal`, beta = -0.3 per m, 48 hours. The `r nrow(first_draw)` available cells of its
first draw, 20 per detected hour, against its `r nrow(animal_presence)` presence draws.*

```{r plot-map-animal, fig.height = 5.6, fig.alt = "Map of one bay of Stoney Lake with one animal's 48-hour true track as a thin dark line over its presence draws, among the receivers that heard it."}
# Count the animal's detections per receiver
heard <- table(study$detections$receiver_serial[study$detections$animal_id ==
                                                  animal])
animal_rx <- study$receivers
animal_rx$detections <- as.integer(heard[animal_rx$receiver_serial])
animal_rx$detections[is.na(animal_rx$detections)] <- 0L
# Zoom to the animal's track, with 600 m round it
view <- list(x = range(animal_track$x) + c(-600, 600),
             y = range(animal_track$y) + c(-600, 600))
in_view <- animal_rx$x >= view$x[1] & animal_rx$x <= view$x[2] &
  animal_rx$y >= view$y[1] & animal_rx$y <= view$y[2]
# Map depth, the presence draws, the true track over them, the receivers,
# then the track's start
ggplot(depth_cells, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = depth_m)) +
  scale_fill_depth() +
  geom_point(data = animal_presence, aes(colour = "Presence draws"), size = 1.3,
             alpha = 0.6, stroke = 0) +
  geom_path(data = animal_track, aes(colour = "True track"), linewidth = 0.3,
            alpha = 0.85) +
  layer_receivers(animal_rx[in_view, ], count = "detections") +
  geom_point(data = animal_track[1, ], aes(colour = "Start"), shape = 21,
             fill = "white", size = 2.6, stroke = 0.8) +
  # A constant mapped to colour gives each mark an entry in the key
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("True track" = "grey10", "Start" = "black",
                                 "Presence draws" = "#F28E2B"),
                      breaks = c("True track", "Start", "Presence draws"),
                      guide = guide_legend(order = 3)) +
  coord_equal(xlim = view$x, ylim = view$y, expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Easting (m, UTM 17N)", y = "Northing (m, UTM 17N)") +

```

*The same animal in its bay over the 48 hours, with its true track.*

## Stack and fit

`used_available()` stacks the presence draws and the available cells into one table per animal,
one stratum per hour and draw, with bottom depth read at each cell:

```{r stack}
# Stack used and available points with bottom depth
stacked <- lapply(names(available), function(id) {
  used_available(presence[presence$animal_id == id, ], available[[id]],
                 depth)
})
names(stacked) <- names(available)
head(stacked[["selection-01"]], 3)
table(case = stacked[["selection-01"]]$case)[c("1", "0")]
```

A conditional logit on each draw's strata, pooled over the 20 draws with Rubin's rules, gives
one coefficient per animal; the true points against the same available cells give the
coefficient the positions should reach:

```{r fit}
# Fit each draw, then pool: mean estimate; within plus between variance
pool <- function(points) {
  fits <- sapply(1:20, function(m) {
    fit <- clogit(case ~ depth_m + strata(stratum),
                  data = points[points$draw == m, ])
    c(coef(fit), vcov(fit))
  })
  c(estimate = mean(fits[1, ]),
    se = sqrt(mean(fits[2, ]) + (1 + 1 / 20) * var(fits[1, ])))
}
from_positions <- t(sapply(stacked, pool))
from_truth <- t(sapply(names(available), function(id) {
  tag <- study$tags[study$tags$animal_id == id, ]
  used <- truth[truth$animal_id == id, ]
  pool(used_available(used, sample_available(used, coverage$hour, lake,
                                             n = 20,
                                             seed = 100 + tag$replicate),
                      depth))
}))
head(round(cbind(truth = from_truth[, "estimate"],
                 positions = from_positions[, "estimate"]), 3), 3)
```

```{r plot-animals, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Per-animal coefficient from position draws against the coefficient from the true track, with 95% intervals."}
# Coefficient per animal: true track against position draws
tags <- study$tags[match(rownames(from_truth), study$tags$animal_id), ]
animals <- data.frame(tags[c("animal_id", "beta")],
                      truth = from_truth[, "estimate"],
                      truth_se = from_truth[, "se"],
                      positions = from_positions[, "estimate"],
                      positions_se = from_positions[, "se"])
animals$group <- ifelse(animals$beta == 0, "beta 0", "beta -0.3")
ggplot(animals, aes(truth, positions, shape = group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
              colour = "grey40") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = positions - 1.96 * positions_se,
                    ymax = positions + 1.96 * positions_se),
                colour = "#2C5AA0", alpha = 0.35, width = 0) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = truth - 1.96 * truth_se,
                    xmax = truth + 1.96 * truth_se),
                colour = "grey45", alpha = 0.35, width = 0,
                orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(colour = "#2C5AA0", fill = "#2C5AA0", size = 2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`beta -0.3` = 21, `beta 0` = 1),
                     name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Coefficient from the true track (per m)",
       y = "Coefficient from position draws (per m)") +
  theme_positionr() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

*Depth coefficient of each animal, with 95% intervals. Dashed line, equal coefficients.*

```{r between-count, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# Animals with a negative true-track coefficient whose positions fall
# between it and zero
negative <- animals$truth < 0
between <- negative & animals$positions > animals$truth &
  animals$positions <= 0
```

Of the `r sum(negative)` animals with a negative coefficient on the true track,
`r sum(between)` have a position coefficient between it and zero. These are the trial's
coefficients for the 40 animals; the trial below reports the mean over animals.

## Use against availability: the trial

```{r lake-scale, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# True-track coefficient over beta at -0.3 and +0.3, both blocks, sorted
trial <- study$trial
lake_scale <- unlist(lapply(c(-0.3, 0.3), function(beta) {
  sort(sapply(1:2, function(b) {
    rows <- trial[trial$block == b & trial$receivers == 70 &
                    trial$availability == "weighted" & trial$beta == beta &
                    trial$source == "truth", ]
    mean(rows$estimate) / beta
  }))
}))
```

The coefficient is a lake-scale use-availability slope. On the true track it is `r ratio(lake_scale[1])` to
`r ratio(lake_scale[2])` of beta at -0.3 and `r ratio(lake_scale[3])` to
`r ratio(lake_scale[4])` at +0.3, below the per-step preference the simulation gave.

```{r trial-table}
# Population mean of per-animal coefficients with a t interval over animals
population <- function(rows) {
  half <- qt(0.975, nrow(rows) - 1) * sd(rows$estimate) / sqrt(nrow(rows))
  c(mean = mean(rows$estimate), lower = mean(rows$estimate) - half,
    upper = mean(rows$estimate) + half, animals = nrow(rows))
}
# Ratio of mean positions to mean truth, with a paired bootstrap over animals
ratio_ci <- function(rows) {
  both <- merge(rows[rows$source == "truth", c("animal", "estimate")],
                rows[rows$source == "positions", c("animal", "estimate")],
                by = "animal", suffixes = c("_truth", "_positions"))
  boot <- withr::with_seed(4, replicate(2000, {
    k <- sample.int(nrow(both), replace = TRUE)
    mean(both$estimate_positions[k]) / mean(both$estimate_truth[k])
  }))
  c(ratio = mean(both$estimate_positions) / mean(both$estimate_truth),
    quantile(boot, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE))
}
trial <- study$trial
scenarios <- unique(trial[c("block", "receivers", "availability", "beta")])
results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(k) {
  s <- scenarios[k, ]
  rows <- merge(trial, s)
  data.frame(s,
             t(setNames(population(rows[rows$source == "truth", ]),
                        c("truth", "truth_lower", "truth_upper", "animals"))),
             t(setNames(population(rows[rows$source == "positions", ])[1:3],
                        c("positions", "positions_lower", "positions_upper"))),
             t(setNames(ratio_ci(rows), c("ratio", "ratio_lower",
                                          "ratio_upper"))))
}))
# A ratio is shown where the true track's interval excludes zero
detected <- results$truth_lower > 0 | results$truth_upper < 0
results[!detected | results$beta == 0,
        c("ratio", "ratio_lower", "ratio_upper")] <- NA
nrow(results)
```

```{r trial-print, echo = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# The 70- and 20-receiver rows under hourly weighting, both blocks
cell <- function(x, lo, hi, f = dec) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf("%s (%s, %s)", f(x), f(lo), f(hi)))
}
shown <- results[results$availability == "weighted", ]
shown <- shown[order(-shown$receivers, shown$beta, shown$block), ]
block_cols <- function(b) {
  d <- shown[shown$block == b, ]
  data.frame(truth = cell(d$truth, d$truth_lower, d$truth_upper),
             positions = cell(d$positions, d$positions_lower,
                              d$positions_upper),
             ratio = cell(d$ratio, d$ratio_lower, d$ratio_upper, ratio),
             n = d$animals)
}
key <- shown[shown$block == 1, c("receivers", "beta")]
table_out <- cbind(key, block_cols(1), block_cols(2))
names(table_out) <- c("Receivers", "beta", "Truth, block 1",
                      "Positions, block 1", "Ratio, block 1", "n",
                      "Truth, block 2", "Positions, block 2",
                      "Ratio, block 2", "n")
knitr::kable(table_out, row.names = FALSE, align = "rrllrrllrr")
```

*The trial, 48 hours, availability weighted by hourly detection. Mean over animals of the
coefficient for bottom depth (per m) with its 95% t interval. Ratio, positions over truth, with
a paired bootstrap interval, shown where the truth interval excludes 0. n, animals heard. Block
2 repeats the trial with its own 100 animals, 20 at each preference; within a block the five
preferences share start cells.*

```{r trial-numbers, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# Numbers the prose quotes, read from the table above
row_of <- function(b, rec, beta, av = "weighted") {
  results[results$block == b & results$receivers == rec &
            results$availability == av & results$beta == beta, ]
}
# The paired difference, positions minus truth, per animal
paired <- function(b, beta, rec = 70) {
  rows <- trial[trial$block == b & trial$receivers == rec &
                  trial$availability == "weighted" & trial$beta == beta, ]
  both <- merge(rows[rows$source == "truth", c("animal", "estimate")],
                rows[rows$source == "positions", c("animal", "estimate")],
                by = "animal")
  mean(both$estimate.y - both$estimate.x)
}
# 20 receivers: animals with no fit that warned of separation
clean <- trial[trial$receivers == 20 & trial$availability == "weighted" &
                 trial$beta == -0.3, ]
clean_animals <- function(b) {
  d <- clean[clean$block == b, ]
  ok <- intersect(d$animal[d$source == "truth" & !d$warned],
                  d$animal[d$source == "positions" & !d$warned])
  d <- d[d$animal %in% ok, ]
  truth_est <- d$estimate[d$source == "truth"][order(d$animal[d$source ==
                                                                "truth"])]
  pos_est <- d$estimate[d$source == "positions"][order(d$animal[d$source ==
                                                                  "positions"])]
  c(animals = length(ok), ratio = mean(pos_est) / mean(truth_est),
    wrong_sign = sum(truth_est < 0 & pos_est > 0))
}
sparse_clean <- lapply(1:2, clean_animals)
```

- **A shallow preference is underestimated from positions.** At beta = -0.3 the position
  coefficient is `r ratio(row_of(1, 70, -0.3)$ratio)` of the true track's in block 1 and
  `r ratio(row_of(2, 70, -0.3)$ratio)` in block 2, with bootstrap intervals that reach
  `r ratio(max(row_of(1, 70, -0.3)$ratio_upper, row_of(2, 70, -0.3)$ratio_upper))` at most.
  A weak shallow preference (beta = -0.1) shows on the true track and not in the positions.
- **At zero preference the positions are closer to zero than the true track.** Paired by
  animal, the draws add `r dec(paired(1, 0))` per m toward deep water in block 1 and
  `r dec(paired(2, 0))` in block 2. With availability weighted by the per-transmission
  probability, positionR 1.x's weight, both intervals exclude zero in both blocks.
- **A deep preference comes back near its size, because the deep shift offsets the
  attenuation.** At beta = +0.3 the ratio is `r ratio(row_of(1, 70, 0.3)$ratio)` in block 1,
  where the position interval includes zero, and `r ratio(row_of(2, 70, 0.3)$ratio)` in
  block 2. Paired, positions minus truth is `r dec(paired(1, 0.3))` per m at +0.3 against
  `r dec(paired(1, -0.3))` at -0.3.
- **On 20 receivers the positions are strongly attenuated.** Among animals with no separated
  fit at -0.3, `r sparse_clean[[1]][["wrong_sign"]]` of `r sparse_clean[[1]][["animals"]]` in
  block 1 come back with the wrong sign.

## Recommendations

- Trust the sign before the size for a shallow preference: positions return about half of it,
  and a weak one can vanish.
- Pass hourly coverage, `system_de(transmissions = )` with the transmissions of one bin, to
  `sample_available()`: an hour is a presence when the animal was heard at least once in it.
  The per-transmission weight showed a preference the animals did not have, in both blocks.
- Use a dense array. On 20 receivers this analysis does not hold up; on 70,
  `r example_single` of the example's `r format(example_hours, big.mark = ",")` detected hours
  were heard by one receiver. Not tested: arrays between 20 and 70 receivers, and penalised
  fits for separation.

## Limits

- The covariate is bottom depth; the simulated walk has no swimming depth and no diel pattern.
- Surfaces exist only for detected hours, so the analysis describes those hours.
- `de_logistic()` is a stand-in for a study's own fitted range model, here the curve the
  detections were simulated from; a wrong curve moves the surfaces and the weight together.
